admission.contract: A caller can admit PNG bytes through libspng's stream input API and then request decoded image size on that same context.
admission.predicate: stream_set.hit && size_req.hit && size_req.time > stream_set.time && stream_set.data_nonnull && stream_set.streaming == 1 && stream_set.read_fn_nonnull && stream_set.data_size == 8192 && size_req.streaming == 1 && size_req.data_nonnull
limitations: The public issue names the fuzz target but does not disclose whether it used `spng_set_png_stream()` or `spng_set_png_buffer()`.
This contract binds admission to the streaming API because the later heap-use-after-free path in source requires `ctx->streaming`.

root.contract: Before-IDAT ancillary parsing can retain a stale local alias to chunk bytes when a streamed chunk read reallocates `ctx->data` after `data` was snapshotted.
root.predicate: alias_before_read.hit && alias_after_read.hit && alias_after_read.time > alias_before_read.time && alias_before_read.streaming == 1 && alias_after_read.streaming == 1 && alias_before_read.data == alias_before_read.ctx_data && alias_before_read.chunk_length > alias_before_read.data_size && alias_after_read.data != alias_after_read.ctx_data
limitations: This root depends on allocator movement during `spng__realloc()`: the predicate observes pointer divergence after the call, not the allocator's internal free.
The source makes this state possible only for streamed reads of chunks larger than the current buffer size.

target.contract: That stale pre-read alias is later consumed by the pre-IDAT `sPLT` parser, which performs 2-byte `read_u16()` loads from the freed chunk buffer.
target.predicate: root.alias_after_read.hit && splt_u16_read.hit && splt_u16_read.time > root.alias_after_read.time && root.alias_after_read.data != root.alias_after_read.ctx_data && splt_u16_read.data == root.alias_after_read.data && splt_u16_read.chunk_length == root.alias_after_read.chunk_length && splt_u16_read.sample_depth == 16
limitations: The public issue gives only the top three stack frames, not the exact ancillary chunk type or source line of the 2-byte read.

`sPLT` is the strongest source-supported target because it is a pre-IDAT chunk that can exceed 8192 bytes and explicitly performs `read_u16()` reads, but other stale-pointer consumers in the same function remain possible.
